name: addpipe24_carry_skip4
rationale: All prior custom adders used full-width prefix/CLA networks that add area but still lose ~0.1-0.17ns of WNS versus the tool-inferred baseline, while pure ripple has the best area but far worse WNS (24-deep serial chain). This design uses a single-level carry-skip structure: six literal 4-bit ripple blocks compute real per-bit sums from the true incoming block carry (guaranteeing bit-exact correctness), while each block also computes a cheap 4-input AND block-propagate signal that muxes the block carry-out directly from the block carry-in when all four bits propagate. Since Pblk=1 mathematically forces the ripple-computed carry-out to equal the carry-in anyway (g_i=0 whenever p_i=1), this mux path is provably value-identical to the ripple result but offers a much shorter alternate physical path for the inter-block carry, letting synthesis bypass slow chains through all-propagate blocks. This should cut the worst-case carry-chain depth roughly in half versus pure ripple (approx block+skip*4+block ~16 stages vs 24) while adding only 6 AND4 + 5 MUX2 cells beyond the ripple baseline, targeting a new non-dominated area/WNS point between the ripple seed (385.168/6.164) and Han-Carlson (469.49/7.345) that the current frontier does not cover.
